use: Siege artillery: a stone-thrower on the Roman side, beyond the board's west edge, in the sieges.

generator.prompt: A Roman onager, a one-armed torsion stone-thrower: a heavy rectangular timber frame lying on the ground, about three metres long, with a thick horizontal bundle of twisted rope in its middle from which a single wooden throwing arm rises, a leather sling at the arm's tip, a padded buffer beam across the front uprights, a winch with spoked handles at the back, and a few round dressed stone balls beside it. Weathered timber, rope and iron. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and strong readable silhouette, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High, before and after
review.notes: A heavy rectangular timber frame on the ground with a long coil of twisted rope along it, a single throwing arm standing upright at its front with a short crossbar at the top and a rope hanging from it, iron fittings and three dressed stone balls beside it; the padded buffer beam the prompt asked for is missing, and the front beam carries a decorative iron plate. The arm stands at the model's -x, so it turns half round (yaw pi) to face east.
